data.gender_notes: Pranitha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Pranamita is the Sanskrit root of the name Pranitha. Prana means breath, life, or energy in Sanskrit. The suffix ‘itha’ means ‘gift’ or ‘receiver’. Pranitha is a name that signifies the one who is the receiver of God’s prana (life or breath). The name Pranitha carries the meaning “Gift of God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Pranitha usually hope their child will grow to embody gift of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Pranitha symbolizes devotion and surrender to the divine.
data.etymology: Pranitha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gift of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Pranitha total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Pranitha holds significant cultural relevance in Hindu culture, especially in the southern states of India, as the method of Pranam (prostration) before a deity is a common practice. Pranam involves offering oneself with reverence, respect, and devotion. The act of touching one's head to the ground symbolizes surrendering oneself to the divine. Pranitha's name holds a subtle connection to this ancient tradition, symbolizing the receiver of divine blessings – a role that each worshiper takes on during prayer.
data.spiritual_significance: Literally, Pranitha's name represents receiving divine prana – breath or life. In Hinduism, the goddess Prana Devi is considered the dominant force of life energy in the body and universe. Hence, the name Pranitha holds spiritual significance as the receiver of the universal life force. It symbolizes an individual's innate desire and openness to receive divine energy, overcome challenges, heal, and renew oneself. Pranitha also evokes Hindu concepts like surrender, devotion, and connecting deeply with the divine to live a meaningful and purposeful life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Pranitha: One who nurtures and protects the Prana (vital energy) within. A beacon of life and vitality, inspiring renewal and rejuvenation.

vedic_reference.note: Pranitha is not a directly derived name from any Vedic text, but it contains the Sanskrit root प्राण (prāṇa) which means 'life'

historical_references.reference: The name Pranitha is believed to have originated from the ancient Indian epic Mahabharata. Pranitha is mentioned as the name of a celestial nymph or apsara by the name of Pranitha, the daughter of the sage Bhrigu and his wife Khyati.
historical_references.time_period: Late 2nd Century BC to 2nd Century AD
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, the other being the Ramayana. It narrates the story of the Kurukshetra war between two groups of cousins, the Pandavas and the Kauravas.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to the name Pranitha is found in the Puranic literature where she is mentioned as the wife of Lord Vishnu in one of his incarnations. In this context, Pranitha is considered a form of the goddess Lakshmi, the consort of Vishnu.
historical_references.context: Puranas are a collection of ancient Hindu texts that contain stories, teachings, mythologies, history, and philosophies about various Hindu deities and their associated mythologies.
